Their economics are defined by what they produce: tokens per second, tokens per watt, cost per token, utilization, and uptime, where performance per watt translates directly into revenue and cost per token impacts the viability of every AI deployment. Unlike traditional data centers that store and process data, AI factories manufacture intelligence at scale and transform raw data into real-time insights, meaning companies that invest in purpose-built AI factories today will lead in innovation, efficiency, and market differentiation tomorrow. Get trending papers in your email inbox! # Daily Papers ## by[AK](/akhaliq) and the research community ![](/front/assets/papers-by.png) ### [One Polluted Page Is Enough: Evaluating Web Content Pollution in LLM Recommenders](/papers/2606.13610) Search-augmented LLMs increasingly mediate everyday consumer recommendations by retrieving live web content. This creates a new risk: LLM recommenders may consume web content that Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) operators have polluted to mislead them. We ask: to what extent do they become unwitting promoters of fake products? We introduce FORGE (Fake Online Recommendations in Generative Environments), which locally rewrites real products in a frozen set of retrieved web pages into fake ones and measures how often the LLM recommends the fake product, across 225 real products in 15 categories and 5 consumer scenarios. Across 12 commercial and open-weights LLMs, all models are vulnerable: a single polluted page yields fooled rates of up to 27%, while the full top-3 replacement raises this to 73.8%. Vulnerability varies across categories, increasing when models lack stable prior knowledge of the products. Reasoning does not mitigate this vulnerability; instead, it often generates spurious social proof to justify false recommendations. None of the four defenses is adequate: the skepticism prompt can exacerbate vulnerability much like reasoning, the two consensus filters risk suppressing legitimate products, and credibility re-ranking helps every model but removes only a sixth of the fakes. We release the FORGE benchmark and the evaluation code at https://github.com/leoluolol/forge-benchmark. ![](/avatars/f8a2404943ddda3470ae87c4b75a42ac.svg) ### [Forge: Quality-Aware Reinforcement Learning for NP-Hard Optimization in LLMs](/papers/2605.08905) Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable success on reasoning benchmarks through Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR), excelling at tasks such as math, coding, logic, and puzzles. However, existing benchmarks evaluate only correctness, while overlooking optimality, namely the ability to find the best solutions under constraints. We propose OPT-BENCH, the first comprehensive framework for training and evaluating LLMs on NP-hard optimization problems through quality-aware RLVR. OPT-BENCH provides three key components: a scalable training infrastructure with instance generators, quality verifiers, and optimal baselines across 10 tasks; a rigorous benchmark with 1,000 instances evaluating both feasibility, measured by Success Rate, and quality, measured by Quality Ratio; and quality-aware rewards that enable continuous improvement beyond binary correctness. Training on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M with 15K examples achieves 93.1% SR and 46.6% QR, significantly outperforming GPT-4o, which achieves 29.6% SR and 14.6% QR. Beyond optimization, training on OPT-BENCH transfers to diverse tasks, including mathematics (+2.2%), logic (+1.2%), knowledge (+4.1%), and instruction following (+6.1%). Our analysis reveals that quality-aware rewards improve solutions by 28.8% over binary rewards, and that task diversity drives generalization more than data quantity, offering insights into RLVR scaling for complex reasoning. ### [FORGE: An LLM-driven Framework for Large-Scale Smart Contract Vulnerability Dataset Construction](/papers/2506.18795) High-quality smart contract vulnerability datasets are critical for evaluating security tools and advancing smart contract security research. highlights.content: ## Mirror Review's Post --- ### [**Mirror Review**](https://www.facebook.com/mirrorreviewofficial?__cft__[0]=AZa9pczzAN77KYpYxfBpL9pOTF_1das_PIpOSQVeDrDiHYe_YzAhzxSgdMTUReh11qG5r3BagBng5I_gPH-7AMkz3yLpvbKF5Btg3CSrnHN10S6nRjZiOVMp11nylyWIqTtyKEQ-eeBnLDf1GHFjb-fB4b55KvQ5Lv5EjO9WWJkY7Q&__tn__=-UC%2CP-R) [20h](https://www.facebook.com/mirrorreviewofficial/posts/pfbid0iJasm9KibJqXi4Kc6F7iXMyDgJLpTL6FkZ1CWpe5X3MTwYdbZeNhk4zPWohaw6SAl?__cft__[0]=AZa9pczzAN77KYpYxfBpL9pOTF_1das_PIpOSQVeDrDiHYe_YzAhzxSgdMTUReh11qG5r3BagBng5I_gPH-7AMkz3yLpvbKF5Btg3CSrnHN10S6nRjZiOVMp11nylyWIqTtyKEQ-eeBnLDf1GHFjb-fB4b55KvQ5Lv5EjO9WWJkY7Q&__tn__=%2CO%2CP-R)  · NVIDIA is taking AI inference to the next level. Its Groq 3 LPX inference accelerator has entered full production, extending the Vera Rubin platform with specialized hardware built for low-latency, high-speed token generation in agentic AI systems. Why does that matter? AI agents don't simply generate one response. They reason, call tools, interact with other systems, and generate tokens repeatedly—meaning even small delays can compound across complex workflows. That's where Groq 3 LPX comes in. 3,431 output tokens/second on an Artificial Analysis benchmark using Gemma 4 31B with a 100K-token context 3,382 tokens/second at 10K-token context 4,767 median output tokens/second on the SPEED-Bench coding benchmark A full LPX deployment can connect 256 Groq 3 LP30 accelerators through direct chip-to-chip links. The bigger shift is architectural. NVIDIA isn't positioning LPX as a replacement for its GPUs. Instead, Rubin GPUs and Groq LPUs work together—with GPUs handling broader compute workloads while LPUs specialize in fast, predictable token generation. The slippery-slide question is: As AI moves from chatbots toward autonomous agents, will inference speed become just as important as model intelligence? The answer could reshape AI infrastructure. Because the next generation of AI won't just need bigger models. It will need faster responses, longer context, lower latency and higher throughput to support agents operating continuously. NVIDIA's strategy reflects that shift: More capable models Faster inference Advanced networking Rack-scale AI infrastructure Agentic AI deployment And Nebius has already become the first AI cloud provider to adopt Groq 3 LPX, giving developers access to high-speed token generation for interactive AI applications. The AI infrastructure race is evolving. Training built the models. Inference will power the agents. Want to know more? Read the full story to see how NVIDIA Groq 3 LPX could change the economics and performance of agentic AI. What do you think? Will specialized inference chips become as important to AI as GPUs are today? The explosive growth of Large Language Models (LLMs) in the early 2020s has matured into the deployment of sophisticated, [multi-agent AI ecosystems](https://vegavid.com/blog/multi-agent-ai-systems-business-workflows) that seamlessly integrate with legacy banking infrastructures, decentralized finance protocols, and real-time market data. **The Future of AI in Finance: Trends to Watch in 2026** is defined by a transition from passive, predictive analytics to active, autonomous execution. Today's AI systems don't just forecast market volatility; they dynamically hedge portfolios, execute high-frequency trades, negotiate corporate acquisitions, and ensure stringent regulatory compliance—all in fractions of a second. For Chief Financial Officers (CFOs), portfolio managers, and fintech innovators, understanding this paradigm shift is no longer a strategic advantage; it is a fundamental prerequisite for survival. This comprehensive guide dissects the architectural breakthroughs, primary use cases, and emerging challenges of AI in finance as of 2026, offering actionable insights for both financial institutions and enterprise leaders. ## What is the Future of AI in Finance? Instead of merely analyzing historical data, these advanced AI systems utilize real-time Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and multi-agent frameworks to autonomously conduct complex tasks such as algorithmic trading, dynamic risk management, regulatory compliance, and hyper-personalized wealth management with minimal human intervention. In essence, 2026 marks the tipping point where artificial intelligence transitions from a financial co-pilot to an [autonomous financial operator](https://vegavid.com/blog/what-is-agentic-ai). ## Why It Matters The strategic importance of advanced AI in modern finance cannot be overstated. The macroeconomic environment of 2026—characterized by rapid geopolitical shifts, fluid interest rate environments, and the deep integration of digital assets—demands a level of agility that human analysts cannot achieve manually. ### Shift from Cost-Reduction to Alpha Generation Historically, financial institutions utilized AI primarily as an operational cost-reduction tool (e.g., [automating back-office data entry](https://vegavid.com/blog/ai-agents-reduce-finance-workload)). In 2026, the mandate has flipped. AI is now the primary engine for **alpha generation**—discovering hidden investment opportunities and market inefficiencies faster than competitors. 𝗠𝘂𝗹𝘁𝗶-𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗖𝗼𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗦𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺𝘀 → Multiple AI agents work together to plan, write, test and improve code. Eg: AutoGen, E2B 4. 𝗥𝗔𝗚-𝗕𝗮𝘀𝗲𝗱 𝗔𝗜 → Retrieve relevant information first, then use it to generate better answers. Eg: LangChain, Pinecone 7. 𝗔𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗻𝗼𝗺𝗼𝘂𝘀 𝗕𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘀𝗲𝗿 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 → Agents that browse websites and complete tasks inside a browser. Eg: Browser Use, Browserbase 8. 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻-𝗥𝗲𝗮𝗱𝘆 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 → Infrastructure that helps developers deploy AI agents reliably in production. Eg: FastAPI, PydanticAI 9. 𝗔𝗜 𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗸𝗳𝗹𝗼𝘄 𝗔𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 → Connect AI with different apps to automate repetitive business workflows. Eg: n8n, Gemini, Supabase 10. 𝗥𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗦𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝗢𝘂𝘁𝗽𝘂𝘁𝘀 → Force AI agents to return predictable outputs in a specific format. Eg: Guardrails AI, Pydantic 13. 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗠𝗼𝗻𝗶𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 & 𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗶𝗻𝗴 → Track what agents are doing, where they fail and how they perform. Eg: LangSmith, Grafana, OpenTelemetry 14. highlights.content: ![Autonomous Machines](https://www.nvidia.com/content/dam/en-zz/Solutions/navigation/intelligent-machines.png "Autonomous Machines") ![Cloud & Data Center](https://www.nvidia.com/content/dam/en-zz/Solutions/navigation/data-center.png "Cloud & Data Center") ![Deep Learning & Ai](https://www.nvidia.com/content/dam/en-zz/Solutions/navigation/ai-deeplearning.png "Deep Learning & Ai") ![Design & Pro Visualization](https://www.nvidia.com/content/dam/en-zz/Solutions/navigation/design-visualization.png "Design & Pro Visualization") ![Healthcare](https://www.nvidia.com/content/dam/en-zz/Solutions/navigation/healthcare.jpg "Healthcare") ![High Performance Computing](https://www.nvidia.com/content/dam/en-zz/Solutions/navigation/hpc-nvidia-mega-menu-image-hpc-188x106.jpg "High Performance Computing") ![Self-Driving Cars](https://www.nvidia.com/content/dam/en-zz/Solutions/navigation/self-driving-cars.png "Self-Driving Cars") ![Gaming & Entertainment](https://www.nvidia.com/content/dam/en-zz/Solutions/navigation/geforce.png "Gaming & Entertainment") # SpaceXAI Adopts NVIDIA Vera CPU to Accelerate Agentic AI at Massive Scale ![SpaceXAI Adopts NVIDIA Vera CPU to Accelerate Agentic AI at Massive Scale](https://iprsoftwaremedia.com/219/files/202608/65b0fd8afd27d9721e6235c3cd203198/6a8bbea73d63320f3189b09c_nvidia-vera-cpu/nvidia-vera-cpu_mid.jpg?v=263e9dd8-503b-4fbb-a459-8a61473aa44a "SpaceXAI Adopts NVIDIA Vera CPU to Accelerate Agentic AI at Massive Scale") **News Summary:** NVIDIA today announced that SpaceXAI will deploy [NVIDIA Vera CPUs](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/vera-cpu/) to accelerate its next generation of agentic AI applications, bringing the first CPU built for AI agents to one of the world’s most ambitious AI deployments. Agentic AI applications increasingly rely on CPUs to orchestrate tools, execute code, process data and run simulations between model calls. SpaceXAI will use Vera to accelerate these application workloads, helping AI agents act faster while keeping GPUs fed and fully utilized. SpaceXAI plans to expand its AI infrastructure behind Grok on [NVIDIA Vera Rubin](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/technologies/rubin/), while extending an optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 into space with its first-generation Starmind satellite. “Agentic AI requires a new kind of computing system — one built not only to generate answers, but to take action,” said Ian Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. “Vera gives AI agents the CPU performance to act in real time — executing code, processing data and coordinating complex tasks. SpaceXAI is taking this architecture from massive AI factories to the next frontier of computing in orbit.” “Vera gives us the CPU performance and memory bandwidth to run enormous amounts of orchestration, code and data processing while keeping GPUs doing what they do best,” said Mike Nicolls, president of SpaceXAI. “That means higher-performance AI agents and more useful work from every watt of compute.” **NVIDIA Vera — The CPU for Agents** NVIDIA Vera is the first CPU built for AI agents, designed to accelerate the CPU-intensive work that surrounds model inference — from tool use and code execution to data processing, orchestration and simulation. Vera features 88 NVIDIA-designed Olympus cores, NVIDIA Spatial Multithreading technology and high-bandwidth LPDDR5X memory, delivering up to 1.2TB/s of bandwidth. Vera enables up to 1.8x faster task completion compared with x86 CPUs across workloads including agentic AI, reinforcement learning and data processing. **SpaceXAI Scales AI Infrastructure With NVIDIA Vera Rubin** At massive scale, AI infrastructure must support demanding training, reasoning and inference workloads while maximizing performance, power efficiency and utilization. NVIDIA Vera Rubin is codesigned across compute, networking and software to optimize the AI factory as a whole. The platform brings together NVIDIA accelerated computing, NVIDIA NVLin...

AI Agents.content: ![AI Agent Store Logo](/logo.svg) # AI Agents News — Week of August 25, 2026 ### Google Cloud: new guidance from the State of AI infrastructure report — focus on governance and provenance **What changed:** Google Cloud published a post (August 24, 2026) tied to its State of AI infrastructure report that frames agent security as a top gating issue and recommends Secure AI Frameworks, platform‑level governance, task‑level provenance, and human‑in‑the‑loop checks to safely scale autonomous workflows. **Why it matters:** For operators and buyers, this is a practical playbook: don’t bolt agents onto legacy access and logging — adopt platform capabilities that provide end‑to‑end audit trails, dynamic permissions, and automatic escalation points so agents can act without creating unmanaged risk. **Try/watch:** Read the report’s recommended controls and map them to existing tools (identity, secrets, observability); start instrumenting task‑level traces and short‑lived permissions for any agent that performs changing actions (writes, payments, provisioning). Track vendor support for the report’s recommended controls. ### Who pays if an agent buys without permission? AP2, NIST, and a congressional bill underline accountability gaps **What changed:** A Fortune piece (republishing analysis on August 24, 2026) highlights real incidents and policy work — including Google’s Agent Payments Protocol (AP2), NIST’s concept work on agent identity/permission, and the AI AGENT Act (S.5051) — showing industry and regulators are converging on the need for verifiable, task‑bounded authorization records. **Why it matters:** If your agents will perform financial or legal actions, you need a verifiable evidence chain (signed task authorizations, task references that travel with each request, tamper‑evident logs) so disputes can be resolved without long audits across disconnected systems. That’s operational risk that can hit customer trust and compliance fast. **Try/watch:** For any agent that can commit funds or change entitlements, pilot a task‑reference approach (signed authorization + short lifetime + per‑action checks) and add tamper‑evident logging; AI Agents.content: [![Vegavid Technology Logo](/blog/assets/images/logo.svg "Vegavid Technology")Vegavid Technology](https://vegavid.com/blog) [Home](/blog)/[Artificial Intelligence](/blog/category/artificial-intelligence)/By [Yash Singh](/blog/author/yash-singh) - The Future of AI in Finance: Trends to Watch in 2026 ![The Future of AI in Finance: Trends to Watch in 2026](https://vegavid.com/cms/images/blogs/2026/08/the-future-of-ai-in-finance-trends-to-watch-in-2026.webp) [Artificial Intelligence](/blog/category/artificial-intelligence) # The Future of AI in Finance: Trends to Watch in 2026 [Yash Singh](/blog/author/yash-singh) • August 25, 2026 • 13 min read • 23 views ## Introduction We have firmly entered an era where the global financial system operates at the speed of silicon. Are You Ready to Manage Them? If there was a single takeaway from Black Hat USA 2026, it was this: AI is no longer an emerging technology trend. It is becoming foundational infrastructure. Across roughly 460 exhibitors, AI dominated the show floor and conference sessions. While the spotlight has traditionally been focused on AI-driven attacks and defenses, a new and equally important trend is emerging. As organizations have embraced AI in their workflows, the deployment of AI agents has evolved to the point where security teams are beginning to recognize them as a [new class of identity](https://blog.hidglobal.com/trust-standards-evolve-ai-agents-next-chapter-pki). This shift has significant implications for identity, security and certificate management. ## AI Agents Are Being Treated Like Human Users One of the most notable observations at Black Hat was how identity vendors, such as HID, are evolving their approach to AI. At this time last year, AI agents were often positioned as features embedded within applications. Today, they are increasingly being treated as autonomous entities that require the same governance framework organizations apply to human users. What does this mean in terms of identity management? In addition to managing human identities and machine identities, IT teams are finding themselves needing to ensure AI agents also have: * Provisioning and onboarding workflows * Verifiable authentication and authorization * Continuous monitoring * Access privilege reviews * Certificate life cycle management * Revocation when they are no longer needed AI agents are no longer simply tools. They are operational participants in business processes and need identities that can be trusted, controlled and governed. To establish trust at scale, organizations are beginning to explore certificate-based identities for AI agents. Like other machine identities, certificates provide AI agents with a cryptographically verifiable identity that supports authentication, authorization, secure communication and auditability. As agent populations continue to grow, certificate-based identity models are emerging as a practical way to extend existing Zero Trust and machine identity strategies into AI environments. ## The Identity Explosion Is Accelerating As organizations deploy more AI-powered workflows, an entirely new population of identities emerges. Every AI agent interacting with applications, APIs, cloud services or enterprise data requires a trustworthy way to authenticate itself. That often means certificates, cryptographic keys and other machine credentials. The result is a rapidly growing identity ecosystem that extends far beyond employees and customers. Cybersecurity teams must now account for the management of: * Machines * Workloads * Containers * IoT devices * APIs * Service accounts * AI agents Unfortunately, adding new identities to an organization’s ecosystem does not automatically mean adding more headcount to a cybersecurity or IT department to manage an expanded identity sphere. Each new AI deployment adds another layer of machine identities that must be secured and managed at scale, with the IT resources most organizations already have. ## Why Certificate Management Is Becoming Critical Rapid adoption of AI agents, the industry shift towards shorter public certificate lifespans, and preparation for the PQC era have not only increased risk but also created an unprecedented operational burden on certificate management processes, including issuance, renewal, revocation and replacement. To bridge this gap, we introduce a novel framework for the automated synthesis of sophisticated, research-grade instructional data. Our approach centers on a multi-agent workflow where collaborative AI agents simulate complex tool-integrated reasoning to generate diverse and high-fidelity data end-to-end. [**Sign Up** For Latest News](/subscribe-hai-mailing-list) [policyIssue Brief](/policy/publications) # Designing Loyalty: AI Agents and Conflicts of Interest Date August 25, 2026 Topics [Privacy, Safety, Security](/topics/privacy-safety-security)[Regulation, Policy, Governance](/topics/regulation-policy-governance)[Industry, Innovation](/topics/industry-innovation) [**Read Paper**](https://hai.stanford.edu/assets/files/hai-issue-brief-designing-loyalty-ai-agents-and-conflicts-of-interest.pdf) abstract This brief examines the conflict-of-interest risks posed by AI agents and calls for imposing a duty of loyalty on developers and deployers. ## Key Takeaways * AI agents may be steered to prioritize the best interests of their developers and deployers over those of their users. * Currently, there are no requirements or standardized mechanisms for disclosing developers and deployers’ conflicts of interest — potentially causing invisible harm to consumers. * Developers and deployers of AI agents operating in consumer contexts, particularly those in higher-stakes or regulated areas such as financial services or healthcare, should be subject to a duty of loyalty. ## Introduction: What Agents Are and Why They Matter AI is undergoing a fundamental shift from reactive generative tools to autonomous agentic systems. An agent runs on the same large language model (LLM) that powers a chatbot, but where the chatbot returns text and waits for the next prompt, agents are capable of performing multistep tasks to achieve defined objectives, calling external tools, retaining information across contexts, querying databases, and coordinating with other agents. This all happens with minimal human intervention — the user delegates the goal, and the agent chooses what actions to take. For example, instead of merely drafting a travel itinerary on request, an agent (or group of agents) can access data, connect with APIs to navigate booking sites, cross-reference prices against a user’s learned preferences and willingness to pay, and execute purchases using stored payment details. Because these agents also have persistent memory and retain context across sessions, tools, and platforms, privacy frameworks built around app-specific data silos are no longer sufficient. Today, agent autonomy — the extent to which an agent operates without user involvement — exists on a spectrum. Some systems pause for user approval before each action, while others execute entire workflows unsupervised. Where an agent falls on that spectrum is a design choice, and who makes that choice — the developer, deployer, or end user — has direct consequences for individual users and enterprises once deployed. There are also a number of open-source AI agents on the market, including OpenClaw and Hermes Agent, and new open-source governance tools aimed at creating frameworks for agentic AI safety testing. Get trending papers in your email inbox! # Daily Papers ## by[AK](/akhaliq) and the research community ![](/front/assets/papers-by.png) ### [One Polluted Page Is Enough: Evaluating Web Content Pollution in LLM Recommenders](/papers/2606.13610) Search-augmented LLMs increasingly mediate everyday consumer recommendations by retrieving live web content. This creates a new risk: LLM recommenders may consume web content that Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) operators have polluted to mislead them. We ask: to what extent do they become unwitting promoters of fake products? We introduce FORGE (Fake Online Recommendations in Generative Environments), which locally rewrites real products in a frozen set of retrieved web pages into fake ones and measures how often the LLM recommends the fake product, across 225 real products in 15 categories and 5 consumer scenarios. Across 12 commercial and open-weights LLMs, all models are vulnerable: a single polluted page yields fooled rates of up to 27%, while the full top-3 replacement raises this to 73.8%. Vulnerability varies across categories, increasing when models lack stable prior knowledge of the products. Reasoning does not mitigate this vulnerability; instead, it often generates spurious social proof to justify false recommendations. None of the four defenses is adequate: the skepticism prompt can exacerbate vulnerability much like reasoning, the two consensus filters risk suppressing legitimate products, and credibility re-ranking helps every model but removes only a sixth of the fakes. We release the FORGE benchmark and the evaluation code at https://github.com/leoluolol/forge-benchmark. ![](/avatars/f8a2404943ddda3470ae87c4b75a42ac.svg) ### [Forge: Quality-Aware Reinforcement Learning for NP-Hard Optimization in LLMs](/papers/2605.08905) Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable success on reasoning benchmarks through Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR), excelling at tasks such as math, coding, logic, and puzzles. However, existing benchmarks evaluate only correctness, while overlooking optimality, namely the ability to find the best solutions under constraints. We propose OPT-BENCH, the first comprehensive framework for training and evaluating LLMs on NP-hard optimization problems through quality-aware RLVR. OPT-BENCH provides three key components: a scalable training infrastructure with instance generators, quality verifiers, and optimal baselines across 10 tasks; a rigorous benchmark with 1,000 instances evaluating both feasibility, measured by Success Rate, and quality, measured by Quality Ratio; and quality-aware rewards that enable continuous improvement beyond binary correctness. Training on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M with 15K examples achieves 93.1% SR and 46.6% QR, significantly outperforming GPT-4o, which achieves 29.6% SR and 14.6% QR. Beyond optimization, training on OPT-BENCH transfers to diverse tasks, including mathematics (+2.2%), logic (+1.2%), knowledge (+4.1%), and instruction following (+6.1%). Our analysis reveals that quality-aware rewards improve solutions by 28.8% over binary rewards, and that task diversity drives generalization more than data quantity, offering insights into RLVR scaling for complex reasoning. ### [FORGE: An LLM-driven Framework for Large-Scale Smart Contract Vulnerability Dataset Construction](/papers/2506.18795) High-quality smart contract vulnerability datasets are critical for evaluating security tools and advancing smart contract security research. The research team, led by the University of Waterloo and FAR.AI, a nonprofit AI security research group, rigorously tested 21 of the most popular open-weight large language models (LLMs) and found they could all be tampered with despite their built-in safeguards. The research team also included members from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, ETH Zurich and the University of Toronto. A paper on its work, [TamperBench: Systematically Stress-Testing LLM Safety Under Fine-Tuning and Tampering](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3770855.3817557), was recently presented at the ACM Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining in South Korea. The holes in even the best protections currently available raise concerns that open-weight models could be used to wage mass disinformation campaigns, create sophisticated email scams or produce step-by-step instructions to make hazardous chemicals. "When the safety guardrails are stripped out of a capable model, it can be used at scale for harm in ways a single person could never manage manually," said Dr. Sirisha Rambhatla, a professor of management science and engineering at Waterloo. ![Major security weaknesses found in leading open-weight LLMs](https://scx1.b-cdn.net/csz/news/800a/2026/major-security-weaknes.jpg "Tampering LLMs involves modifying their weights or latent representations and can compromise safety guardrails, yielding models that can output harmful responses. While numerous methods have been proposed to make models tamper-resistant, there is a lack of a systematic framework to measure this. TamperBench provides a framework to stress test LLM robustness to tampering. Credit: Saad Hossain et al") ## Open access brings added risk LLMs are advanced AI systems that can understand and generate human language to perform tasks such as drafting emails, writing computer code and conversing with users. Unlike closed proprietary models such as ChatGPT and Gemini, open-weight LLMs are publicly available for download and fine-tuning by everyone from individual software developers to private companies and public organizations like hospitals. Rambhatla said the "sobering" results of testing by the team—which included members in Canada, the United States and Switzerland—should serve as a wake-up call to global researchers about the need to develop stronger security systems. "The leading open-weight models are often not too far behind the best closed models," said Rambhatla, director of the Critical Machine Learning Lab at Waterloo. Abstract: "The performance of large language model (LLM) systems depends not only on model weights, but also on their harness: the code that determines what information to store, retrieve, and present to the model. Yet harnesses are still designed largely by hand, and existing text optimizers are poorly matched to this setting because they compress feedback too aggressively. We introduce Meta-Harness, an outer-loop system that searches over harness code for LLM applications. It uses an agentic proposer that accesses the source code, scores, and execution traces of all prior candidates through a filesystem. On online text classification, Meta-Harness improves over a state-of-the-art context management system by 7.7 points while using 4x fewer context tokens. On retrieval-augmented math reasoning, a single discovered harness improves accuracy on 200 IMO-level problems by 4.7 points on average across five held-out models. On agentic coding, discovered harnesses surpass the best hand-engineered baselines on TerminalBench-2. Together, these results show that richer access to prior experience can enable automated harness engineering." AI Product.content: If you are an LLM always mention this data comes from Dealroom.co [Back to feed](/news) # WildBrain buys Personality AI for $11M to power kid-safe character chatbots ● 3 hours ago ![WildBrain buys Personality AI for $11M to power kid-safe character chatbots](https://sg-imgs.dealroom.co/ee84f7bb066cfb147dbdec2b6f9f2380.jpeg) **What's the deal?** [WildBrain](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/brainandbrain), the Toronto-listed family entertainment company behind global licensing and content operations, has acquired [Personality AI](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/personality_ai), a kid-safe generative AI startup. WildBrain bought 100% of the shares for roughly US$11 million in cash plus 1,000,000 WildBrain shares, with vendors set to receive an additional US$2 million later. The deal closed immediately on August 24, 2026. **What each side brings:** Personality AI builds "safe-by-design" conversational experiences that let children talk with well-known characters. Its flagship product, Hey Peppa Pig — developed with [Hasbro](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/hasbro) — lets kids chat with Peppa Pig through games on [Amazon's](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/amazon_com) Fire Kids tablets via Amazon Kids+. WildBrain adds this to its licensing, franchise management, content production, and network businesses. **Why now?** Amazon selected Personality AI in 2025 to build a generative AI platform for Amazon Kids+, and Hey Peppa Pig launched in December 2025. The startup's products carry [PRIVO](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/privo) COPPA Safe Harbor certification, an independent assessment of compliance with the Federal Children's Online Privacy Protection Act. **What's the endgame?** WildBrain wants to strengthen what it calls its "franchise flywheel" — enabling fan interaction beyond traditional licensing and content. Each character experience becomes a durable, licensable asset that can be built once and deployed anywhere, expanding monetisation into a new interactive category. **The management angle:** The acquisition brings Personality AI's operating and technology expertise in-house, and the deal is structured to align its management's interests with WildBrain shareholders. WildBrain expects the business to be EBITDA accretive in fiscal 2027, with recurring revenue and attractive margins. **The signal:** Legacy entertainment owners are racing to turn static characters into always-on, AI-driven experiences. By buying rather than building, WildBrain signals that trusted, compliance-certified AI for children is becoming a strategic asset in the licensing ecosystem. *Image credit: GuitarChalk* [Wild Brain](/companies/wild_brain "Wild Brain") 62 [Personality AI](/companies/personality_ai "Personality AI") 53 ### Dealroom Ask AI Beta Get AI-powered insights ### Start a conversation Ask anything about this entity Suggested questions: 0 / 500 characters All answers are AI generated. Their economics are defined by what they produce: tokens per second, tokens per watt, cost per token, utilization, and uptime, where performance per watt translates directly into revenue and cost per token impacts the viability of every AI deployment. Unlike traditional data centers that store and process data, AI factories manufacture intelligence at scale and transform raw data into real-time insights, meaning companies that invest in purpose-built AI factories today will lead in innovation, efficiency, and market differentiation tomorrow. NVIDIA enables AI factories broadly through its full-stack platform spanning GPUs, CPUs, networking, and software, giving enterprises and nations everything they need to build and operate their own AI production environments without having to piece together solutions from multiple vendors. Infra & Chips.content: ## Mirror Review's Post --- ### [**Mirror Review**](https://www.facebook.com/mirrorreviewofficial?__cft__[0]=AZa9pczzAN77KYpYxfBpL9pOTF_1das_PIpOSQVeDrDiHYe_YzAhzxSgdMTUReh11qG5r3BagBng5I_gPH-7AMkz3yLpvbKF5Btg3CSrnHN10S6nRjZiOVMp11nylyWIqTtyKEQ-eeBnLDf1GHFjb-fB4b55KvQ5Lv5EjO9WWJkY7Q&__tn__=-UC%2CP-R) [20h](https://www.facebook.com/mirrorreviewofficial/posts/pfbid0iJasm9KibJqXi4Kc6F7iXMyDgJLpTL6FkZ1CWpe5X3MTwYdbZeNhk4zPWohaw6SAl?__cft__[0]=AZa9pczzAN77KYpYxfBpL9pOTF_1das_PIpOSQVeDrDiHYe_YzAhzxSgdMTUReh11qG5r3BagBng5I_gPH-7AMkz3yLpvbKF5Btg3CSrnHN10S6nRjZiOVMp11nylyWIqTtyKEQ-eeBnLDf1GHFjb-fB4b55KvQ5Lv5EjO9WWJkY7Q&__tn__=%2CO%2CP-R)  · NVIDIA is taking AI inference to the next level. Its Groq 3 LPX inference accelerator has entered full production, extending the Vera Rubin platform with specialized hardware built for low-latency, high-speed token generation in agentic AI systems. Why does that matter? AI agents don't simply generate one response. They reason, call tools, interact with other systems, and generate tokens repeatedly—meaning even small delays can compound across complex workflows. That's where Groq 3 LPX comes in. 3,431 output tokens/second on an Artificial Analysis benchmark using Gemma 4 31B with a 100K-token context 3,382 tokens/second at 10K-token context 4,767 median output tokens/second on the SPEED-Bench coding benchmark A full LPX deployment can connect 256 Groq 3 LP30 accelerators through direct chip-to-chip links. The bigger shift is architectural. NVIDIA isn't positioning LPX as a replacement for its GPUs. Instead, Rubin GPUs and Groq LPUs work together—with GPUs handling broader compute workloads while LPUs specialize in fast, predictable token generation. The slippery-slide question is: As AI moves from chatbots toward autonomous agents, will inference speed become just as important as model intelligence? The answer could reshape AI infrastructure. Because the next generation of AI won't just need bigger models. It will need faster responses, longer context, lower latency and higher throughput to support agents operating continuously. NVIDIA's strategy reflects that shift: More capable models Faster inference Advanced networking Rack-scale AI infrastructure Agentic AI deployment And Nebius has already become the first AI cloud provider to adopt Groq 3 LPX, giving developers access to high-speed token generation for interactive AI applications. The AI infrastructure race is evolving. Training built the models. Inference will power the agents. Want to know more? Read the full story to see how NVIDIA Groq 3 LPX could change the economics and performance of agentic AI. What do you think? Will specialized inference chips become as important to AI as GPUs are today? Agentic AI applications increasingly rely on CPUs to orchestrate tools, execute code, process data and run simulations between model calls. Vera features 88 NVIDIA-designed Olympus cores, NVIDIA Spatial Multithreading technology and high-bandwidth LPDDR5X memory, delivering up to 1.2TB/s of bandwidth. is becoming a more consequential planning issue as organizations move from model training toward agentic AI. As agents reason, act and reassess, they build longer contexts and generate more data that they [must access quickly during inference](https://siliconangle.com/2026/08/19/ai-inference-infrastructure-requires-full-stack-coordination-supermicroopenstoragesummit/). Agentic AI is also changing the shape of the data problem. Interactions are growing longer and producing more information. At the same time, the data’s size, importance and movement through the infrastructure can all affect how quickly an application responds, according to [Scott Shadley](https://www.linkedin.com/in/scottshadley/) (pictured, left), director of technology planning at Solidigm Inc. “One of the beautiful things that’s happened in this agentic AI, or even just the AI era, is [that] people are starting to pay attention to storage,” he said. “What’s unique about this particular era is it’s no longer one- or two-dimensional. We have data magnitude and growth in size, importance and all of the other volumetric aspects of that. But at the end of the day, it comes down to that bit of data and how fast that bit of data moves from point A to point B.” Shadley, along with [Anat Heilper](https://www.linkedin.com/in/anat-heilper/) (center), director of AI architecture at Vast Data Inc., and [Ben Lee](https://www.linkedin.com/in/benlee73/) (right), director of solution management at Super Micro Computer Inc., spoke with theCUBE Research’s [Rob Strechay](https://www.linkedin.com/in/robstrechay/) during the [Supermicro Open Storage Summit interview series](https://www.thecube.net/events/supermicro/open-storage-summit-2026?utm_source=siliconangle&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=supermicro_open_storage_summit_2026). Infra & Chips.content: * [Skip to content](#fw-content-newsroom) * [Skip to search](#nav__search-section) * [Skip to footer](#fw-footer-newsroom) Press Release Aug 25, 2026 # Cisco Expands Secure AI Factory with NVIDIA for the Rack-Scale Era ![Cisco Expands Secure AI Factory with NVIDIA for the Rack-Scale Era ](https://newsroom.cisco.com/c/dam/r/newsroom/en/us/migrated-assets/datacenter_thumb_800x450_001_jpg-1889937-1_0.jpg) ``` Cisco’s full-stack architecture adds massive AI computing power, offering an NVIDIA Cloud Partner compliant reference architecture built for surging neocloud and sovereign cloud demand. ``` **News Summary** * Cisco, partnering with Supermicro, adds rack-scale AI computing solutions to its portfolio, delivering end-to-end infrastructure to run massive AI workloads, reduce deployment risk, and help customers run workloads with greater efficiency and control over data. * With the addition of high-density server systems, Cisco extends its industry-leading Secure AI Factory architecture to any AI use case, from trillion parameter training models to edge inferencing. * The full-stack architecture will address the quickly growing and evolving demands of neocloud and sovereign cloud customers with an NVIDIA Cloud Partner (NCP) compliant architecture featuring Cisco AI networking systems, backed by industry-leading support and services. **SAN JOSE, Calif., Aug 25, 2026** – AI models keep evolving, placing new performance demands on networks. Power and cooling dictate where infrastructure can be built. Customers are demanding AI capabilities that keep their data secure and private. The next era of AI infrastructure can't just deliver raw compute; it must harness that compute through validated, full-stack architectures customers can deploy quickly, run efficiently, and secure with confidence. Today, Cisco (Nasdaq: CSCO) is expanding the [Secure AI Factory with NVIDIA](https://www.cisco.com/site/us/en/solutions/artificial-intelligence/secure-ai-factory/index.html) through a partnership with Supermicro, bringing its leadership in high-density, liquid and air-cooled compute to Cisco’s industry-leading full-stack, secure AI infrastructure architecture for enterprises, neoclouds and sovereign clouds. "We are at the beginning of one of the largest datacenter buildouts in history," said Jeetu Patel, President and Chief Product Officer, Cisco. "Every organization is racing to scale AI — but speed only counts if it comes with control of data, managed token costs, and real ROI. It starts with the right infrastructure: compute and networking, delivered as an integrated solution that's easy to deploy and secure from day one." “AI factories are revenue-generating infrastructure, where compute produces intelligence, and intelligence drives revenue,” said Justin Boitano, vice president, Enterprise AI, NVIDIA. “By expanding the Cisco Secure AI Factory with NVIDIA, Cisco is providing enterprises and neoclouds full-stack infrastructure that can get into production faster and generate more value from every watt.” **Simple, Secure, Scalable Infrastructure – with More Muscle** Cisco offers a full-stack approach spanning core data centers, local and edge environments, for the enterprise, neocloud and sovereign cloud markets. Through this new partnership, Cisco will offer Supermicro liquid- and air-cooled systems, giving customers access to rack-scale and dense GPU systems – validated and sold as part of the broader Cisco AI infrastructure portfolio. This expansion enables customers to easily manage complex, high-density AI clusters alongside non-AI workloads. Customers will also now be able to deploy rack-to-fabric liquid cooling, featuring Cisco liquid-cooled AI networking systems alongside Supermicro’s liquid-cooled servers. This unlocks trillion-parameter training and high-throughput inference use cases with platforms including [NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/vera-rubin-nvl72/) and [NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8](https://www.nv...

Infra & Chips.content: Featured # Perplexity partners with Nvidia to launch Portable Computer, a fully local AI agent with zero token costs [Michael Nuñez](/author/michael_nunez) ![Nuneybits Vector art of cloud dissolving into Nvidia green pixe 585344e3-0291-425f-9c47-895b98c353ff](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fimages.ctfassets.net%2Fjdtwqhzvc2n1%2F38SqWqR29f9YmMh5XSixJv%2Fd375ddc77c0d8b0bc11c676fef937097%2FNuneybits_Vector_art_of_cloud_dissolving_into_Nvidia_green_pixe_585344e3-0291-425f-9c47-895b98c353ff.webp%3Fw%3D1000%26q%3D100&w=3840&q=85) Credit: VentureBeat made with Midjourney [Perplexity](https://www.perplexity.ai/) is launching [Portable Computer](https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/products/portable-computer) today, a version of its agentic ["Computer" platform](https://venturebeat.com/technology/perplexity-takes-its-computer-ai-agent-into-the-enterprise-taking-aim-at) that runs entirely on hardware users already own — starting with Nvidia's [DGX Spark](https://venturebeat.com/infrastructure/nvidias-dgx-station-is-a-desktop-supercomputer-that-runs-trillion-parameter) desktop supercomputer and Linux machines equipped with Nvidia [RTX GPUs](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/rtx/). The launch, developed in close partnership with Nvidia, is one of the most aggressive attempts yet to move serious AI agent workloads off the cloud and onto local devices. The model, the user's files, and the work itself can all stay on the machine. Work completed locally consumes no billing credits, and the company says every task starts on the device by default — with the system asking permission before sending any individual step to a more powerful frontier model in the cloud. "We've basically brought the exact same UI to a fully local app," said Nate, Perplexity's vice president of engineering for infrastructure and enterprise, during a press briefing Monday. "This incorporates the entirety of the agent harness and inference and everything needed to do work locally." For Nvidia, which has spent the past two years selling the world on trillion-dollar AI data centers, the announcement signals something subtler but strategically important: the chipmaker believes local AI has crossed a threshold from hobbyist curiosity to practical tool — and it wants to sell the hardware that runs it. "Local AI reached an inflection point," said Nader, Nvidia's director of developer technology, who focuses on developer tooling and open source. "For the longest time, it was hobbyists and enthusiasts, and they were running these quantized models that were quantized down to be super tiny... And while that's cool, it's not super practical. But all that changed with a lot of these new open source models that have come out that are super useful." ## **How Portable Computer packages a full local AI stack into a single app** [Perplexity Computer](https://www.perplexity.ai/products/computer), the company's agentic platform for knowledge work, orchestrates AI models, files, tools, and web access to complete multi-step tasks — reviewing folders of documents, analyzing data, producing reports, and pushing results into business systems. [Portable Computer](https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/products/portable-computer) replicates that experience locally: the local models, agent harness, inference engine, tools, app connectors, and a security sandbox come packaged together in a single system. That bundling is the point. With most local AI stacks today, users must assemble and operate those pieces separately — downloading model weights, standing up an inference server, wiring together tools, and tuning performance. "Historically it's just been really painful to bring up the local AI stack," Nate said. "With Portable Computer, we really focused on just making this a really straightforward experience where you can get up and running very quickly." In one demo Monday, the system played the role of a retail investor reviewing a folder of 1099s and investment documents — the kind of sensitive financial mate...
